subject.title: Intermittent 30+ minute workspace-sandbox prep on cold-start (5.19-beta.1)

question: Should OpenClaw fix this class with a default Docker control-plane timeout and fail-soft sandbox unavailability behavior, or keep waiting for a narrower live repro before changing sandbox defaults?
rationale: The source-level hang is clear, but the final timeout value, config exposure, fail-soft semantics, and coverage of prune/hash/setup paths affect existing slow Docker setups and need owner intent.

options.title: Complete the timeout/fail-soft fix
options.body: Refresh or replace the open timeout PR, cover prune/hash/init waits, require real Docker/OrbStack proof, and document any public default or config surface before merge.

options.title: Accept a narrower mitigation
options.body: Land only the per-call Docker init timeout after maintainers explicitly accept the remaining prune/hash/live-proof gaps and slow-Docker behavior change.

options.title: Hold for live reproduction
options.body: Keep the issue open without merging timeout behavior until reporter logs or maintainer-run OrbStack proof isolates the slow substep more precisely.

recommendation.title: Complete the timeout/fail-soft fix
recommendation.body: Refresh or replace the open timeout PR, cover prune/hash/init waits, require real Docker/OrbStack proof, and document any public default or config surface before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Docker sandbox helper, config, and spawn-related history makes this the strongest routing candidate for the default/compatibility choice.
